document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Deny They Are Sheltering HUA Militants, Usama bin Laden (Islama 09517)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Ambassador Simons presses Taliban acting foreign minister Mullah Ghaus on HUA militants in Khost camps and bin Laden near Jalalabad. Ghaus denies any foreigners are in Khost and suggests bin Laden left with Hekmatyar. The page adds 9/11 Commission context on bin Laden's return and Pakistani intelligence facilitation.

TALIBAN "ACTING FOREIGN MINISTER" MULLAH MOHAMMED GHAUS
THERE ARE NO FOREIGNERS IN KHOST PROVINCE--ONLY TALIBAN.

events.description: Ambassador Simons met Taliban acting FM Ghaus, raised HUA in Khost and bin Laden in Jalalabad; Ghaus denied both.
The News published article alleging HUA militants training in two camps vacated by Afghan Arabs in Khost.
US Embassy Islamabad cabled State reporting the meeting and doubting Taliban candor.
Ambassador Simons raised HUA sheltering and bin Laden's whereabouts with Ghaus; Ghaus denied both.
The News article alleged HUA militants training in two camps vacated by Afghan Arabs in Khost.
Embassy Islamabad cable reporting the Taliban denial.
US warned HUA may soon be designated a terrorist organization.

key_claims: The Taliban acting foreign minister Ghaus denied that HUA militants or bin Laden were in Taliban-controlled areas.
Ghaus claimed Hekmatyar invited bin Laden to Afghanistan and that bin Laden may have left Kabul with him.
US reports mostly placed bin Laden near Jalalabad in Nangarhar.
A Pakistani journalist said Taliban Nangarhar officials told him bin Laden was in Jalalabad.
The Embassy assessed that evidence increasingly suggested the Taliban were not being candid.
The US considered designating HUA a terrorist organization due to its implication in kidnappings of Westerners in Kashmir.
